Q: Who they are Spheros is a US-based seed fintech and data infrastructure company led by co-founder Catherine Outlaw. It is building B2B SaaS and identity-verification infrastructure that lets businesses upload data once and share it with financial institutions. The founders’ relevant experience includes Bank of America and Circle; other details about the team, investment criteria, and business are not known. So far You are connected and have exchanged messages about a potential fit. Spheros said its focus on fintech, B2B SaaS, identity verification, and related services aligns with your stated interest in fintech, B2B SaaS, and enterprise software. A brief meeting is scheduled for Friday at 2:00 p.m. UTC. No prior call or assessment is provided. What they'll likely ask What exactly does Spheros do, and who is the customer? We provide a secure, encrypted data hub where businesses upload information once and share it with institutions such as banks. The stated business model is that banks pay a subscription fee while their clients use the service for free. Your record does not yet show the precise buyer, pricing structure, implementation process, or which workflows are covered first. What traction do you have today? You have secured 10 clients, of which two are paying. You are also in pilot discussions with four of the 20 largest US banks. I would have the names or categories of the clients, contract status, revenue, pilot scope, and conversion timing ready, because those details are not provided. How much time and money does the product save customers? The problem is based on fragmented manual data-sharing processes. The pitch cites McKinsey estimates that banks can take up to 100 days and spend $25,000 onboarding each client. Your record does not show Spheros-specific measured savings, onboarding-time reduction, accuracy improvement, or customer ROI, so I would distinguish the external benchmark from verified customer results. How do you win and retain banks, and what is the competitive position? The product is positioned as a trusted data wallet for sharing information with institutions. Your record does not explain the alternatives customers use today, the competitive set, why banks would adopt Spheros rather than build or use another provider, or how identity verification and security are differentiated. I would answer directly and avoid presenting the positioning as proof of defensibility. How much are you raising, and what will the financing achieve? You are raising $2 million to hire developers and a sales team and onboard 10,000 clients over the next 18 months. Your record does not show the current runway, valuation, committed capital, hiring plan, revenue targets, or the assumptions behind the 10,000-client goal. I would have those figures and milestones ready. Weak spots Early commercial traction is promising but limited: 10 clients are stated, with only two paying, while four large-bank pilots are still discussions. Separate signed customers, active pilots, paying customers, and prospective discussions. Be ready with revenue, contract values, pilot milestones, conversion timing, and references where shareable. Do not treat pilot discussions as secured customers. The pitch relies on broad market benchmarks, but no Spheros-specific customer outcomes are provided. Present the McKinsey figures as context, not as proof of Spheros’ impact. Bring measured onboarding times, costs, usage, customer feedback, and any quantified ROI if available; otherwise say those metrics are not yet established. The product, security model, competition, and route to 10,000 clients are not sufficiently detailed in the material provided. Explain the initial use case, data flows, compliance and security controls, buying process, sales cycle, and the assumptions behind the growth target. Be explicit about what remains to be validated. Your ask Ask what information they need next to assess fit, and whether they would be open to a follow-up focused on traction, bank pilots, security, and the financing plan. Want to rehearse it? I'll play Spheros.
